context.process_name: Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance
context.objective: Document how we carry out Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Oh, it kicks off when someone comes into the fund late, or an investor bumps up their commitment, that kind of thing. It just happens whenever, not on a schedule.
Talk me through what happens after an investor joins late or increases their commitment.
The client sends a close notification, and there is the signed subscription or commitment increase paperwork that comes with it.
What happens next once the close notification and signed paperwork arrive?
Someone on the team opens up the close and does the usual checks to make sure it is ready to go, writes down the basics and stuff.
What do the team’s readiness checks verify before they open the close?

The fund admin preparer confirms the client approved the admission, AML is cleared, and the system and portal onboarding is done. If documents are incomplete or the AML, commitment or effective date records are missing, it gets escalated and no equalization call goes out for that investor.
Once those readiness checks pass, what happens next in the close?
Then they sort out which rules apply, the agreement stuff, with the reviewer and the client or legal chiming in. It gets written up and locked.
How do they determine which agreement rules apply to that close?

The partnership agreement and side letters set the rate, the start and end dates, day count, compounding and who gets the interest, plus which earlier calls count. We never assume any of that, and if it is unclear the work pauses until the client or legal gives written direction.
How do they use those rules to calculate the equalization amount for the investor?

Well, first the preparer pulls together the list of all the earlier capital calls and ties it out, and the reviewer verifies it. Then they work out what the new investor would have put in on each call, and the interest goes on top of that per the agreement.
How do they calculate the interest on each earlier call amount?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

memo_findings.answer: Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance

Work is triggered when an investor enters the fund late or an existing investor increases their commitment. The work occurs whenever one of these events arises, not on a schedule.
The client sends a close notification when the work is initiated. The participant also identifies signed subscription paperwork or signed commitment-increase paperwork as accompanying the notification.
It remains unclear who receives or detects the client’s close notification and accompanying paperwork.

After the notification and paperwork arrive, someone on the team opens the close, checks that it is ready to proceed and writes down the basics.
The basics recorded and their location, and the steps following the described calculation, remain unspecified.
After readiness checks pass, the team determines the applicable agreement rules with the reviewer and input from the client or legal; the rules are written up and locked. If the rules are unclear, work pauses until the client or legal provides written direction.
The fund admin preparer checks admission approval, AML clearance and completed system and portal onboarding. Incomplete documents or missing AML, commitment or effective-date records are escalated, and the investor's equalization call is held.
The preparer gathers and ties out a list of all earlier capital calls, and the reviewer verifies it. Then the team works out what the new investor would have contributed on each call and adds interest under the agreement.

A team member performs readiness checks on the close before proceeding.
The escalation recipient, resolution and evidence of readiness checks remain unspecified.
The fund admin preparer confirms client approval of admission, AML clearance, and completion of system and portal onboarding. Incomplete documents or missing AML, commitment or effective-date records are escalated, and no equalization call goes out for that investor.
The preparer ties out the list of earlier capital calls, and the reviewer verifies the list before the contribution amounts are worked out.
The sources and comparisons used to tie out and verify the earlier-call list are not yet described.

Signed subscription or commitment-increase paperwork accompanies the client's close notification.
The receipt and storage locations for the notification and signed paperwork are not established.
The partnership agreement and side letters provide the reported equalization terms. The applicable rules are written up and locked; client or legal direction is provided in writing when terms are unclear.
The preparer assembles a list of earlier capital calls for the tie-out, review and calculation.
The reported work concerns a fund when an investor joins late or increases a commitment.

The partnership agreement and side letters set the interest rate, start and end dates, day count, compounding, interest recipients and which earlier calls count. The team does not assume these terms; unclear rules pause the work until written direction from the client or legal.
Admission approval, AML clearance and completed system and portal onboarding are readiness conditions; incomplete documents or missing specified records prevent the investor's equalization call from going out.
The calculation works out what the new investor would have contributed on each earlier call, then adds interest according to the agreement.
The equalization work depends on AML clearance and completion of system and portal onboarding before proceeding.
System and portal onboarding must be completed as part of readiness; the systems are not named.

capture.summary: The preparer assembles and ties out earlier calls, the reviewer verifies the list, and the team calculates the new investor’s contributions and agreement-based interest. What does the preparer compare the earlier-call list against when tying it out?
